items.claim: A1 Move by / Rotate by enabled for a selection they can't change
items.note: They now give the answer Transform Again gives, through a new `selectionTransformAnswer` in editing that Transform Again also uses. A locked node is dropped from the batch, so a locked selection reads `NotApplicable`; a locked layer can read `Locked`.

items.claim: A2 the current measurement can be a hidden one
items.note: `currentMeasureId` passes over hidden measurements, and measurements on a hidden layer, using `nodeGates`. That covers the readout, Delete, Move by and Rotate by.

items.claim: A3 a stale pick keeps Deselect Measurement enabled and swallows Escape
items.note: `unpick` is enabled only while the pick is the current measurement, and now declares `requires: ['scene']`.

items.claim: A4 a measurement off its layer still paints and snaps but can't be picked, edited or cleared
items.note: question, recorded as an `Open:` line in `docs/unruled.md` in 666d4514ab. Neither way out is free. Making `measureIds` read the whole scene puts a walk of every node on each pointer move's hit test, which `measureEndSource.test.ts` ("reads only the measurement layer's nodes, not the whole scene") forbids. The other way, having the painter and snap source read only `ms.layer`, leaves that measurement data in the document with nothing drawing it. Which one is a design call.

items.claim: B1 the readout shows the committed measurement during a drag
items.note: The readout reads the node through `shownLookup` and subscribes to `scene.overrides`.

items.claim: B2 the current measurement can be a hidden one
items.note: duplicate of A2, fixed by bc799a18f9.
